newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures, alike, were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Mostly higher cash hog indications and a rise in pork cutout values linked to stronger pork prices were expected to spark carryover demand from Tuesday. Packers were paying up for cash hogs early Wednesday to encourage larger marketings, analysts said.
However, rolling of long June positions into July is expected to continue, keeping a lid on the spot month. Futures are also premium to cash, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index was down $0.91 at $77.40 per cwt while June close Tuesday at 80.775 cents.
Pork belly futures were expected to show carryover demand on a firmer tone to cash bellies late Tuesday, when prices were called steady to higher, and on continued light hog slaughter, analysts said.

However, analysts were divided on the effect of the CME out-of-town storage report. CME reported a net out-movement last week of 137,000 lbs from warehouses outside Chicago versus in movement of 202,000 lbs last year.

Some analysts considered the report mildly bullish as there was an out-movement compared with an in-movement last year but others said the net withdrawal was smaller than anticipated which could weigh on sentiment.
